top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock (Katori and Ye) rests on a distinct idea, a magic wavelength cancelling the lattice light shift for many neutral atoms, and it has been independently reproduced near 1e-18 in several laboratories. It has already opened new physics (redshift tests, constraints on drifting constants and dark matter, many-body effects in the clock). The citation can stay narrow and need not invoke the comb or ion-trap prizes, and the two-name allocation is defensible. This is a mature, confirmed achievement, so an award is better than no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; I chaired the 2025 committee (superconducting circuits) and work on DFT and spin dynamics for MAX IV/ESS, but have no tie to Katori, Ye or the lattice-clock groups
